_comment: Committed target table for the road-to-cost-parity-* family (part 0, Phase 1). Registers what a session costs today, what the family is steering toward, and what the rule payload actually is PER HOST — the correction that matters most, because every diet target in the source drafts was set against one aggregate number that describes no host. Nothing here changes behaviour: no carrier ships for these thresholds (part 0 Phase 4.5), and no gate reads the target columns. What IS gated is the file's own shape — lint_budget_ownership rejects a row without a `source`, and rejects a `revised_from` without `revision_evidence`, so a number cannot enter or move without a traceable origin.

row_schema._comment: Reading of part 0 § 1.2b: `schema_version` / `registered_at` / `owner` / `review_by` are FILE-level (as in every sibling budget file — a per-row copy would be four constants repeated N times), and every ROW carries `source` plus the three honest-null fields from § 1.3. The validator enforces exactly that split.
row_schema.honest_null_contract: A target bends to a measurement, never to a preference. `revisable: true` says the number is revisable at all; `revised_from` records what it used to be once it moves; `revision_evidence` must then point at the evidence note that forced the move. The validator fails the file when `revised_from` is set and `revision_evidence` is empty — a revision without published evidence is the one form of drift this schema exists to refuse.

measurement._comment: Both measurement rules from part 0's Context are fields here, not prose: a rule that lives only in a paragraph is a rule the next author does not inherit.
measurement.regeneration_command: task sync && task generate-tools — verified no-op afterwards (git status clean), so the payload rows below measure the commit and not when someone last ran a generator
measurement.emitter_generation: real, frontmatter-less projection files (25 of 110 .claude/rules entries carry a `paths:` block; the rest carry no frontmatter). NOT the older emitter that symlinked .claude/rules/* into dist/agent-src/rules/ and so inherited dist's full frontmatter. This is the THIRD variable behind the 92-vs-110 file-count spread: a projection count is a fact about which emitter last wrote the tree, on top of how stale that tree is.
measurement.carrier_divergence_reason: report_carrier_divergence compares a globally installed carrier against the project projection on disk; both can be stale independently, so it measures relative cache staleness rather than any property of the source. It may diagnose a behind-the-times install; it may never gate a phase, and no row here is derived from it.

payload_rows._comment: CORRECTION to part 0's triage table, which recorded these two as "~3 KB / ~0 KB" and therefore as already-lean hosts needing no target. Re-measured post-regeneration they are 408 KB and 330 KB — a full payload each. The earlier reading is a stale-projection artefact of exactly the class measurement rule 1 warns about: both carriers are UNTRACKED and written only by `task generate-tools`, so a checkout that has not run it reads them as near-empty. Risk 3's mitigation ("the lean hosts need no target") does not survive the re-measure and is not encoded here.

anchors.rationale: Above ~200k a session sits in the premium pricing band, which is why the median target is set there rather than at a round fraction of the baseline.
anchors.known_noise_problem: 187 of 205 observed sessions end at or above 200k, so a session-end hint at this threshold would fire on ~91% of sessions — a constant line, not an advisory. The 200k figure is a TARGET here and nothing else.
anchors.no_carrier_ships: Part 0 § 4.5: no session-end advisory ships for this anchor. The existing 800k recycle threshold (src/config/recycle-threshold-budget.json) stays the only strong line, and any carrier for 200k is a separate, separately-argued change.
